planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Deutschland is one of the earliest-blooming Georg Arends hybrids, opening well before midsummer arendsii cultivars.

directions: Deutschland is an early-season Georg Arends hybrid astilbe, sending up dense, upright plumes of pure white flowers over a lustrous green foliage mound in late spring to early summer, ahead of most other arendsii cultivars. Its early timing makes it useful for starting the shade border's astilbe bloom sequence before midseason pinks and reds take over. Keep the soil consistently moist and humus-rich in partial to full shade, since dry spells quickly brown the plume tips and stress the foliage. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain a full, floriferous mound.

common_name: Vision in Pink Astilbe (Light Pink Chinensis Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial shade to full shade; Vision in Pink is an early-to-midsummer chinensis selection distinct from the later, more compact Little Vision in Pink.

directions: Vision in Pink is an Astilbe chinensis selection bearing light pink, densely packed plumes over a compact mound of lacy, blue-green foliage, opening in early to midsummer. It is somewhat more tolerant of brief dry spells than many arendsii hybrids, a trait typical of the chinensis group, though it still performs best with steady moisture. Grow in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade, with a bit more sun tolerated in cooler climates. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to keep plumes dense and well colored.

common_name: Maggie Daley Astilbe (Late-Season Lavender Chinensis Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Maggie Daley is a late-blooming chinensis selection that extends the astilbe season into late summer.

directions: Maggie Daley is a late-flowering Astilbe chinensis cultivar producing dense, fuzzy lavender-purple plumes that age to a warm caramel tone, extending interest well after the plumes fade. Because chinensis types bloom later than most arendsii hybrids, it fills a valuable gap at the tail end of the shade border's astilbe season, from midsummer into late summer. Plant in humus-rich soil that stays consistently moist, since dry conditions quickly cause irreversible leaf scorch. Leave the spent caramel plumes standing through fall for winter interest, and divide congested clumps in spring every few years.

common_name: Look at Me Astilbe (Bubblegum-Pink Arendsii Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Look at Me is a compact, heavy-blooming arendsii selection introduced in the Netherlands.

directions: Look at Me is a compact Astilbe x arendsii cultivar bred to put most of its energy into bloom, sending up large, bubblegum-pink plumes on contrasting red stems above a tidy mound of lacy green foliage in early to midsummer. It was recognized as a notable new introduction at the Plantarium trade show in the Netherlands, and its disciplined, floriferous habit suits small borders and containers as well as traditional shade plantings. Grow in rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade, since the plant can tolerate more sun only where summers stay cool. Divide clumps every three to four years in spring to keep flowering dense.
sources: Proven Winners / Plantarium trade show records

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Pink Lightning is a dwarf simplicifolia hybrid suited to the front of the border or rock gardens with reliable moisture.

directions: Pink Lightning is a dwarf Astilbe simplicifolia hybrid forming a low mound of glossy, dark green leaves edged in a darker tone, topped in early summer by loose, arching sprays of pale pink flowers. Its small scale and open, airy flower form set it apart from the stiffer, more upright plumes of arendsii and chinensis cultivars, making it a good fit for small shaded beds or container plantings near water. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in dappled to full shade, since foliage scorches readily in hot sun or dry soil. Divide every few years in spring to refresh vigor.

common_name: Jump and Jive Astilbe (Magenta-Pink Music Series Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Jump and Jive belongs to the Dutch-bred Music series of astilbe and blooms in early to midsummer.

directions: Jump and Jive is an Astilbe x arendsii selection from the Dutch-bred Music series, producing luminous magenta-pink plumes over a glossy, deep green, fern-like foliage mound in early to midsummer. The spent plumes age to a rich caramel color, adding a second season of interest into fall if left standing. Grow in humus-rich soil that never dries out, in partial sun to full shade, since the foliage browns quickly under moisture stress. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to keep the planting full and vigorous.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Snowdrift is a compact, white-flowered arendsii selection suited to small borders.

directions: Snowdrift is a compact Astilbe x arendsii cultivar producing feathery, pure white plumes on upright stems above a tidy mound of lacy green foliage. Its restrained size makes it a practical choice for the front of a shaded border or a mixed container where taller white astilbe cultivars would overwhelm the planting. Grow in rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade, since the plant quickly shows stress in dry conditions. Divide every three to four years in spring to maintain dense, even flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Bonn is an early-to-midseason japonica astilbe with dense carmine-pink plumes.

directions: Bonn is an Astilbe japonica cultivar forming a clump of shiny, deeply divided green foliage beneath long, dense plumes of carmine-pink flowers in late spring to early summer, earlier than most arendsii hybrids. Its japonica parentage gives it a tighter, glossier foliage mound than many arendsii selections, and the spent flower heads age to an attractive brown that persists into winter. Grow in evenly moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, since japonica types are quick to decline in dry soil. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to renew vigor.
